questions.q: Which factor is most important when designing a product to be used by a child aged under 12 months?
questions.explanation: For an infant under 12 months, safety is the overriding design factor because the user cannot recognise or avoid hazards such as choking, sharp edges or toxic materials. Quality, economics and obsolescence are secondary to protecting the end user's wellbeing.

questions.q:
A newly designed can opener was trialled in 200 households.

Which of the following is the most effective strategy for collecting the findings from the households?
options: Ask each household to complete a questionnaire
Visit each household and observe how they use the can opener
Collect reviews on can openers from major consumer websites
questions.explanation: A questionnaire is the most efficient way to gather consistent, comparable primary data from a large sample of 200 households. Interviewing or observing each one is too time-consuming, and website reviews are secondary data about other products, not the trialled prototype.

questions.q:
Designers are still using hand-drawn sketches when developing ideas.

What is an advantage of using a hand-drawn sketch in comparison to using a computer-generated sketch?
options: It is more convenient in expressing initial concepts.
It is more efficient for producing large scale drawings.
questions.explanation: Freehand sketching lets a designer capture and communicate initial concepts quickly and conveniently without setting up software. Higher accuracy, colour range and large-scale efficiency are strengths of computer-generated drawing, not hand sketches.

questions.q:
A new mobile phone cover is to be designed.

To meet the functional requirements of the product, which of the following lists of criteria should be considered?
options: Weight, size and ease of use
Cost, ease of use and being fashionable
questions.explanation: Functional requirements relate to how well the cover performs its job, so weight, size and ease of use are all functional criteria. The other lists mix in aesthetic and economic factors such as colour, attractiveness, cost and being fashionable.

questions.q:
A coffee table has been designed with a touch screen computer built into it.

Which factor is most likely to have influenced this design?
questions.explanation: Building interactive touch-screen technology into furniture responds to social trends in how people use and integrate technology in everyday living. Aesthetic, safety and environmental factors are not the main driver of adding a computer to a coffee table.

questions.q: To develop a product, it is most important to first
questions.explanation: An action plan is developed first because it sequences and schedules the tasks, time and resources needed to manage the whole project. Prototyping and ongoing evaluation occur later, guided by that plan.

questions.q: For an innovation to be successful, it must
options: be launched at an appropriate time.
questions.explanation: A successful innovation must meet a genuine user need, otherwise consumers will not adopt it regardless of marketing. Advertising, trademarks and timing can support an innovation but cannot make a product succeed if it fails to address user needs.

questions.q:
The prototype of a product has been delivered on time and on budget but the client finds the prototype lacking in several expected functions.

What should the designer have done initially to prevent this from happening?
options: Produced a more comprehensive financial plan
Produced additional sketches with the prototype
Conducted a detailed analysis of the design requirements
questions.explanation: The problem is missing functions, which means the design requirements and client criteria were not properly clarified at the start. A detailed analysis of the design requirements would have established exactly what functions the client expected before building the prototype.

questions.q: One benefit of making a prototype prior to construction is that it could
questions.explanation: Building and testing a prototype lets the designer identify and resolve faults before full production, reducing manufacturing risks and costly errors. The other options are not the primary purpose of prototyping.

questions.q: Using a variety of research methods in the process of design is important because it
options: promotes the use of emerging technologies.
protects the intellectual property of the designer.
questions.explanation: Using varied research methods triangulates data from different sources, giving the designer a fuller and more reliable understanding of customer needs. The other options are not the central reason for researching during the design process.

questions.q:
A designer has been asked to produce a working prototype of a desk lamp that uses a variety of materials.

Outline safe work practices that should be implemented by the designer during the development of the prototype.

criteria.descriptor: Outlines safe work practices that should be implemented by the designer with a direct link to the desk lamp
Identifies safe work practices that should be implemented by the designer and outlines at least one of them
Identifies safe work practices OR outlines one safe work practice
Identifies a safe work practice

questions.modelAnswer: A risk assessment should be conducted before constructing the prototype, and personal protective equipment (PPE) used to minimise injury — for example a face mask and eye protection (goggles, safety glasses) to guard against dust and flying particles when cutting wood for the lamp stand, and hearing protection when sawing. Electrical work on the lamp should be carried out and tagged by a licensed technician, and materials should be tested to ensure no toxic fumes are emitted. Tools and machinery should be regularly maintained and inspected, and suitable training (SOP/SLMS and MSDS sheets) undertaken before use.

questions.q:
A team of designers is working together on a design project.

Describe how information storage devices could be used to support the teamwork and collaboration of these designers.

criteria.descriptor: Clearly describes how teamwork and collaboration of the designers is supported by information storage devices
Outlines different ways that teamwork and collaboration of the designers is supported by information storage devices
Outlines how teamwork and collaboration could be supported by information storage devices
Identifies features of teamwork and collaboration and/or information storage devices
Identifies a feature of teamwork and collaboration or an information storage device

questions.modelAnswer: Information stored in digital form on devices such as computer hard drives, USB memory sticks and CDs can be emailed to team members quickly and easily for sharing ideas and gathering feedback, unlike bulky paper-based storage. External hard drives let designers carry larger and greater quantities of files between locations. Files held on a computer network can be password protected, with members assigned different permissions such as read-only or the right to modify. Documents can also be uploaded to the 'cloud' for web-based storage, allowing designers in diverse geographical locations to upload, comment and edit collaboratively in real time, even with virtually unlimited storage space.

questions.q: Explain the legal issues that should be considered by a designer when developing a new technology. Include examples in your answer.

criteria.descriptor: Indicates how and/or why legal issues should be considered when developing a new technology; supports answer with examples
Indicates how and/or why legal issues should be considered when developing a new technology; includes one example
Outlines legal issues and indicates how and/or why for at least one of these issues OR describes legal issues that should be considered when developing a new technology
Outlines legal issues that should be considered when developing a new technology
Identifies legal issues associated with developing a new technology OR outlines a legal issue
Identifies a legal issue associated with developing a new technology

questions.modelAnswer: Because society constantly demands new and innovative designs, designers must protect their new technologies from being copied by obtaining patents, which costs money, time and legal fees that must be budgeted for. A patent prevents others from making, using or selling the invention without permission, but intellectual property rights do not last indefinitely, so renewal fees must be paid promptly and trademark registration kept current. The patent or copyright should be updated when the invention changes so all aspects remain protected. If incorporating another's design, the designer must identify the copyright/patent owner, seek permission and check the scope of any rights granted. Packaging and shape can also be protected — for example the Apple–Samsung lawsuits covered the shape of the iPhone and the colours of the graphical user interface, were lengthy, costly and international (US, Australia, Japan, Germany, South Korea, UK), and infringement could even result in a product being banned from sale. Other legal issues include privacy, meeting safety standards, building codes and government regulations.

questions.q:
Analyse the opportunities and challenges faced by designers when attempting to design and produce sustainable products.

Your answer will be assessed on how well you: demonstrate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question; communicate ideas and information using relevant examples; and present a sustained, logical and cohesive response.

criteria.descriptor: Shows a comprehensive understanding of the opportunities and challenges faced by designers when attempting to design and produce sustainable products; draws out and relates implications of these opportunities and challenges; communicates using relevant examples; responds in a sustained, logical and cohesive manner

Shows a detailed understanding of the opportunities and challenges faced by designers when attempting to design and/or produce sustainable products; explains opportunities and challenges; includes relevant examples; responds in a logical manner
Describes opportunities and challenges faced by designers when attempting to design and produce sustainable products; may include a relevant example
Outlines opportunity(ies) and/or challenge(s) faced by designers
Identifies opportunity(ies) and/or challenge(s) faced by designers

questions.modelAnswer: Designers must consider sustainable products because traditional resources such as fuels and plastics are in decreasing supply. Sustainable products open the opportunity to use a wider range of materials and processes — for example biodegradable plastics such as 'Biopak' packaging reduce waste, particularly at the end of the product's life. This appeals to consumers, so adopting it can widen the consumer base, increase sales and profit, and even shift consumer demand so society expects similar sustainable choices elsewhere. The main challenge, however, is cost: developing sustainable technologies takes time and money and companies must stay financially viable, so in their early introduction sustainable methods are usually more expensive than traditional ones, which keeps many designers using cheaper raw materials such as oil-based petrochemicals. For example, Nike turned waste leather from its SE Asian footwear production into a 'second' raw material to make the 'Nike Trash Talk' shoe, requiring new manufacturing sites and worker retraining that raised costs — so it was only marketed in Europe and the US, while developing economies still demanded traditionally produced, waste-generating footwear. Overall, sustainable products are essential to reduce raw-material extraction and waste, and designers must weigh improved materials and long-term profitability against the short-term costs in order to change global demand and design trends.
